dataset.name: Data and Scripts associated with: “Laboratory evaluation of open source and commercial electrical conductivity sensor precision and accuracy”
description: This data package is associated with the publication “Laboratory evaluation of open source and commercial electrical conductivity sensor precision and accuracy: How do they compare?” submitted to PLOS ONE and accepted for publication (Fulton, S.G. et al. 2023; doi not yet available).

Variation in electrical conductivity (EC) of water is important to reveal environmental disturbance and natural dynamics, including factors such as anthropogenic salinization. This data package supports a study addressing the need for a robust performance assessment of open source (OS) EC sensors. We evaluated the accuracy (mean error, %) and precision (sample standard deviation) of OS EC sensors in the laboratory via comparison to EC calibration standards using three different OS and OS/commercial-hybrid (OS/C) EC sensors and data logger configurations and two commercial (C) EC sensors and data logger configurations. We also evaluated the effect of cable length (7.5 m and 30 m) and sensor calibration on OS sensor accuracy and precision. This data package presents the results from the different testing laboratory configurations. It also includes an R script for statistical analysis of the data and an Arduino IDE file used to calibrate and collect data with the OS Atlas EC sensor. File types are .csv, .pdf, .R, and .ino.

measurementTechnique: We evaluated the accuracy (mean error, %) and precision (sample standard deviation) of open source (OS) electrical conductivity (EC) sensors in the laboratory via comparison to EC calibration standards using three different OS and OS/commercial-hybrid (OS/C) EC sensors and data logger configurations and two commercial (C) EC sensors and data logger configurations. We also evaluated the effect of cable length (7.5 m and 30 m) and sensor calibration on OS sensor accuracy and precision. Prior to collecting EC sensor data, we performed a 2-point calibration according to manufacturer requirements using two different sets of calibration standards: 1) 84 μS/cm and 1413 μS/cm (“narrow calibration”) and 2) 84 μS/cm and 2060 μS/cm (“wide calibration”). EC measurements (μS/cm) were automatically temperature compensated to 25° C (i.e., specific conductance, SC). Three EC measurements were collected following calibration over a 15-min period (one measurement every 5 min) using each sensor configuration. Due to the small sample size and the presence of outliers, we performed Mann Whitney U Tests (Wilcox.test, p = 0.05) using R Studio to determine whether there were statistically significant differences between overall OS Atlas EC sensor mean accuracy and mean precision and the mean accuracy and mean precision of all other sensors combined (OS/C and C). For greater details on the methodology and sensor configurations, please see the “Materials and Methods” section in the manuscript.
